The Movement Strengthening Initiative built cross-movement alliances by intentionally connecting movement actors across national borders and intersecting movements in East Africa. Five participants from Rwanda (including from RNADW) were engaged in the MSI. Through the MSI there were two distinct cross movement dialogues that benefited the participants; (1) Virtual sessions that took place over a month (August) when the 28 participants of the MSI divided into 3 cross movement, cross border groups to organize independently and met for group discussions to engage on Sexuality, Livelihood/ work and Parenting rights. They then came back into a virtual plenary session and shared their collective leanrings which they documented. (2) In person sessions which took place in Kenya in October when the group made field vists to three different movement actors in their spaces and had deep dialog with them (these organisations were: The National Gay and Lesbian Human Rights Commission, Women Spaces africa (Disability justycie focus) and Jinsiangu (focused on intersex, transgender, and Gender Non-Conforming persons). (3) Despite being a cross-movement learning space and capacity building space for activists who work at the intersection of gender, sexuality and disability DSROI EA has also a component of supporting leaders with disabilities. DSROI EA is a space led by women with disabilities in all their diversities. It is a space where women with disabilities thought leadership is recognized and celebrated, but also a space where leaders with disabilities are supported to develop new knowledge content, design sessions on intersectional topics to participants coming both from feminist and disability rights movements. In this edition of DSROI we had sessions co-led by Deaf women activist from Rwanda on Deaf culture - comparative sesion on Deaf culture and gender in 4 countries - Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda and Zimbabwe. We also had a session on cross-movement work with participation of young women with disability from Rwanda with focus on using art.

There were significant transitions within the CREA East Africa (WGG) office, with both the Program Manager and Program Director transitioning out of the organization. These departures created a notable gap, which impacted the flow of work in the East Africa office, particularly as it took some time to fill both positions.
